Keywords: Laude Hymn Marches and Anti Corruption
RagShortTexts: Penitential expectations can unsettle households already facing war and scarcity.
Flagellant processions of 1260 are future events for characters in 1259.

Variants.Content: A priest or lord hearing apocalyptic preaching in 1259 distinguishes present devotion from next year. Repentance sermons can bring neighbours together, while clerics debate who may preach or hear confession. Rulers watch for disorder. No one can yet report a Perugian movement spreading through Italian cities or its assemblies being outlawed. Observers record claims and local responses, leaving the expected turning point unresolved. Households may disagree about the warning and continue ordinary work while waiting for clearer signs.

In 1259 a priest or lord hears repentance sermons and considers their effect. Neighbours may pray together, while clerics debate who may preach or hear confession. Rulers watch for disorder. No one can report a Perugian movement spreading through Italian cities or authorities outlawing its assemblies. Observers record present claims and responses, leaving the expected turning point unresolved.

In 1259 a poor household can hear penitential preaching and fears of divine judgment without knowing what processions the following year will bring. Public acts of devotion may offer fellowship, but also take workers away from fields and workshops. A rumour about impending punishment is a belief circulating among people, not certain knowledge of the future.
